verses.restored: Looking intently at the council, Paul said, Men, siblings, I have conducted myself in all good conscience before the Divine until this day.

familiar.text: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.

verses.restored: The high priest Ananias commanded those standing by him to strike his mouth.

familiar.text: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.

verses.restored: Then Paul said to him, The Divine is about to strike you, whitewashed wall. You sit judging me according to the Law, and violating the Law, command me to be struck?

familiar.text: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

verses.restored: Those standing by said, Do you insult the high priest of the Divine?

familiar.text: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?

verses.restored: Paul said, I did not know, siblings, that he is high priest; for it is written, You shall not speak harmfully of a ruler of your people.

familiar.text: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

verses.restored: Knowing that one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, Paul cried out in the council, Men, siblings, I am a Pharisee, son of Pharisees; concerning hope and resurrection of the dead I am judged.

familiar.text: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

verses.restored: When he said this, a dispute happened between Pharisees and Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.

familiar.text: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

verses.restored: For Sadducees say there is no resurrection, nor messenger, nor spirit; but Pharisees confess both.

familiar.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

verses.restored: A great cry arose, and some scribes of the party of the Pharisees stood and argued strongly, saying, We find nothing harmful in this human. What if a spirit or messenger spoke to him?

familiar.text: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

verses.restored: When a great dispute happened, the commander, fearing Paul might be torn apart by them, commanded the soldiers to go down, snatch him from their midst, and bring him into the barracks.

familiar.text: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.

verses.restored: The following night the Lord stood by him and said, Take courage, for as you bore witness concerning me in Jerusalem, so it is necessary also for you to bear witness in Rome.

familiar.text: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

verses.restored: When day came, the Judeans made a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath, saying neither to eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

familiar.text: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

verses.restored: There were more than forty who made this sworn plot.

familiar.text: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.

verses.restored: They came to the chief priests and elders and said, We have bound ourselves with a curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

familiar.text: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

verses.restored: Now therefore you, with the council, make clear to the commander that he should bring him down to you, as though you are about to examine more accurately the things about him; we are ready to kill him before he draws near.

familiar.text: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.

verses.restored: But the son of Paul's sister heard of the ambush, and coming and entering the barracks, reported it to Paul.

familiar.text: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

verses.restored: Paul called one of the centurions and said, Bring this young man to the commander, for he has something to report to him.

familiar.text: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.

verses.restored: Taking him, he brought him to the commander and says, The prisoner Paul called me and asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to say to you.

familiar.text: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.

verses.restored: The commander took him by the hand, withdrew privately, and inquired, What is it that you have to report to me?

familiar.text: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?

verses.restored: He said, The Judeans agreed to ask you to bring Paul down tomorrow to the council, as though intending to inquire something more accurately about him.

familiar.text: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

verses.restored: Therefore do not be persuaded by them, for more than forty of their men lie in ambush for him, having bound themselves by oath neither to eat nor drink until they have killed him; and now they are ready, awaiting the promise from you.

familiar.text: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.

verses.restored: The commander therefore released the young man, commanding him, Tell no one that you reported these things to me.

familiar.text: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.

verses.restored: Calling two of the centurions, he said, Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, from the third hour of the night;

familiar.text: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

verses.restored: also provide mounts so that, setting Paul upon them, they may bring him safely to Felix the governor.

familiar.text: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

verses.restored: He wrote a letter having this form:

familiar.text: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

verses.restored: Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix, greetings.

familiar.text: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.

verses.restored: This man was seized by the Judeans and was about to be killed by them when I came upon them with the troops and rescued him, having learned that he is Roman.

familiar.text: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

verses.restored: Wishing to know the accusation for which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their council.

familiar.text: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

verses.restored: I found him accused concerning questions of their Law, but having no accusation worthy of death or bonds.

familiar.text: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.restored: When it was disclosed to me that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him to you immediately, also commanding the accusers to speak the things against him before you.

familiar.text: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.

verses.restored: The soldiers therefore, according to what was ordered them, taking Paul, brought him by night to Antipatris.

familiar.text: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

verses.restored: The next day, allowing the horsemen to go on with him, they returned to the barracks.

familiar.text: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

verses.restored: Those entering Caesarea and delivering the letter to the governor also presented Paul to him.

familiar.text: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

verses.restored: Reading it and asking from what province he was, learning that he was from Cilicia,

familiar.text: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;

verses.restored: he said, I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive. He commanded him to be guarded in Herod's praetorium.

familiar.text: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
